e6c2558dd35f707f4d1cc8ec4285d49c74e612aa.summary: A 2015 TrendLabs blog post by Trend Micro senior threat researcher David Sancho describes how malware uses steganography to hide code and command-and-control (C&C) traffic. It cites a DarkComet dropper, seen in November 2014, that hides encrypted code in a bitmap image in its resources. It describes the Morto Trojan sending Base64-encoded C&C commands in DNS responses, the TDSS/Alureon botnet fetching JPG images from popular blogging sites with commands hidden inside, and ShadyRAT hiding commands in HTML comments and in JPG files using LSB encoding. e66c29589f2d77b18611624a8f1f7ac655ab133e.summary: Kaspersky ICS CERT reports Operation SalmonSlalom, which delivers the FatalRAT backdoor to industrial and government organizations in the Asia-Pacific region. Victims receive zip archives disguised as invoices or tax filing applications, sent by email, WeChat and Telegram. The chain abuses the Youdao Cloud Notes service and a Chinese CDN for staging, DLL sideloading through the legitimate DriverAssistant utility and a PureCodec binary, and a logon script for persistence. e66c3e6b12e93b94f0885ef6f8d74cbfa9702bbc.summary: Cisco Talos report on XorDDoS, a Linux DDoS trojan first identified in 2014. Talos observed it spreading from November 2023 to February 2025, with nearly 50 percent of successfully compromised victims in the United States and over 70 percent of attempted attacks targeting the United States. The report describes a new VIP sub-controller and a central controller that manages multiple sub-controllers, and assesses the toolset as a product developed for sale. Talos assesses with high confidence that the operators are Chinese-speaking. Infection relies on SSH brute-force attacks and root…
